title: The Core Operator Relayer's 2-of-5 threshold lets either two-signer organization act alone
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.2.1.2.2.2 describes the Core Operator Relayer Multisig as "jointly controlled by Operational GovOps Soter Labs and the Spark Assets Foundation." Its composition (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.2.1.2.2.2.3) is Soter Labs 2 signers, Spark Assets Foundation 2 signers, Phoenix Labs 1 signer, with a 2-of-5 threshold, and the note that "Phoenix Labs' signer may create and propose transactions; execution requires meeting the 2/5 threshold."

Do the arithmetic and the joint control is nominal. Soter Labs alone holds two signers and can meet a 2-of-5 threshold unilaterally; so can the Spark Assets Foundation. Only Phoenix Labs, with one signer, genuinely needs a partner — which is what the provision about proposing rather than executing makes explicit for that party alone.

The effective permission structure is therefore: two organizations with unilateral execution power, and one with proposal rights only. The three-party composition creates the *appearance* of distributed control while the threshold makes it a two-of-three-parties-may-act-alone arrangement.

Whether that is a flaw depends on intent. If the goal was availability — ensuring routine relaying continues when one organization is unreachable — the configuration achieves it. If the goal was mutual checking between Soter Labs and the Spark Assets Foundation, the threshold does not deliver it, and raising it to 3-of-5 would. The Artifact's own wording ("jointly controlled") suggests the second reading, which makes this a gap between stated and implemented control.
description: Described as jointly controlled by Soter Labs and the Spark Assets Foundation, the multisig gives each of them exactly two of five signers — so joint control is not actually required to execute.
